phishingTest.explanation: Not phishing-resistant: a code captured by a simulated attacker proxy and relayed to the genuine server within its validity window was accepted, because the code carries no origin binding.

replayTest.explanation: Replay rejected: the server advanced its counter past the matched value, so the same code no longer falls inside the look-ahead window.

desynchronisationObservation.explanation: A token 10 presses ahead was accepted and the server resynchronised (counter → 11); a token 11 presses ahead fell outside the look-ahead window and was rejected. Counter desynchronisation beyond the window needs manual resynchronisation (Chapter 2 §2.4.1.3).

bruteForceTest.explanation: After 5 wrong guesses the credential was locked, and the correct code was refused afterwards. An online guesser has at most 5 tries × 11 acceptable value(s) out of 10^6, a success probability of about 5.50e-5 per lockout period.

expiredCodeTest.explanation: HOTP codes have no time-based expiry. An unused code generated 24 h earlier was still accepted; a captured but unused HOTP code stays valid until a later code is used.

securityNotes: Controlled simulations of defined attack scenarios against this implementation; not penetration testing and not a discovery of unknown vulnerabilities.

phishingTest.explanation: Not phishing-resistant: a code captured by a simulated attacker proxy and relayed to the genuine server within its validity window was accepted, because the code carries no origin binding.

replayTest.explanation: Replay rejected: the server records the last accepted time step (RFC 6238 §5.2) and refuses any step not newer than it. With step tracking disabled the identical code was accepted twice, so replay resistance comes from server state, not from the algorithm itself.

desynchronisationObservation.explanation: Clock drift of up to ±30 s (±1 step) was tolerated; drift of ±60 s was rejected. The validation window trades clock tolerance against how long a code stays usable.

bruteForceTest.explanation: After 5 wrong guesses the credential was locked, and the correct code was refused afterwards. An online guesser has at most 5 tries × 3 acceptable value(s) out of 10^6, a success probability of about 1.50e-5 per lockout period.

expiredCodeTest.explanation: A code used 61 s after generation (beyond ±1 step(s) of 30 s) was rejected.
